tasks.old_behavior: safe_strncpy called strncpy(dest, src, size-1) without NULL-checking src. If src was NULL (e.g., empty DHCP SNAME option dhcp-option=66,), strncpy receives NULL and causes segfault (undefined behavior). dest[size-1] was set to \0 but dest[0] was not explicitly zeroed before strncpy.
tasks.new_behavior: safe_strncpy now checks if (src) before calling strncpy; if src is NULL, it returns an empty string (dest[0] = \0). Additionally, dest[0] = dest[size-1] = \0 zeroes both first and last byte before strncpy, providing defense-in-depth. The function contract is documented: "src may be NULL in which case we return an empty string."
tasks.compatibility_reason: Internal utility fix for NULL-safety. For callers that already pass valid non-NULL strings (vast majority of 30+ call sites), behavior is byte-identical after strncpy. For callers that may pass NULL (specifically DHCP SNAME/file code paths via rfc2131.c), behavior changes from crash (segfault) to defined empty-string output. This is a contract relaxation: previously-Undefined input (NULL) now produces defined behavior. No existing correct caller behavior is broken. The dest[0] initialization is a minor side-effect change but matches what strncpy would write for typical non-NULL short strings.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test DHCP option dhcp-option=66, (empty SNAME) and dhcp-boot with empty filename to confirm no crash and correct DHCP response. Test safe_strncpy with NULL src, empty src (""), and normal src to confirm all three paths produce correct null-terminated strings.
